title.narrative: HPN - Cluster 4: Tujenge Jamii-FP/RMNCAH, WASH and Nutrition (Nakuru County)

description.narrative: (Kenya): Using FY 2022 funds, USAID will continue its support for the Tujenge Jamii activity to increase the use of quality county-led health services in Nakuru County through a service delivery systems approach. Specifically, the activity will strengthen Nakuru county health systems by:.Building the capacity of county and sub-county health managers on leadership management, accountability and governance to enhance ownership and reduce donor dependency.Creating awareness within counties on domestic resource mobilization approaches and ring fencing of health budgets, so as to increase and secure health related budgets.Improving access to antenatal care and skilled birth attendance through advancing universal health coverage by increasing the number of health facilities enrolled in Linda Mama/Free Maternity Services rolled out by the National Health Insurance Fund among rural populations.Improving health information systems to provide quality and timely data in the District Health Information Software 2 package.Supporting the county in building strong integrated commodity supply systems at facility, sub- county and county levels.FY 2022 funds will also support improved access to safe point-of-use water treatment, movement along the sanitation ladder and increased adoption of key hygiene behaviors as well as infection prevention infrastructure in health facilities in accordance with Ministry of Health and USAID standards. To that end, activities will build capacity at the community and facility levels for the prevention and case management of diarrhea and pneumonia as well as efforts to improve child and maternal nutrition.Ultimately, the activity will enable counties to expand access to and the use of voluntary family planning; antenatal care; emergency obstetric and newborn care; postnatal care for mothers and babies; nutrition and routine immunization.
